title: [recoverability] Two backup keys, part B2: the store reads each manifest with the key its object names, puts every file whole after another key's manifest, refuses without that key, and records sealed_with
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 116 [recoverability]: two backup keys, part B2. `spawn store` opens the newest manifest with the key its object names. After a manifest of another key it puts every file whole under the sealing key. Without the other key's file it refuses. Its record says `sealed_with`.

Notes from review: each run adds two or three LIST or GET requests (the newest manifest's key and header). store get on a k2-only host still needs SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY=k2, because Settings::with_r2 requires the sealing key's file (114).

Read crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/store.rs (command, Store::newest, put, rebuild, verify, put_verb, name_key), sync/design-backup-two-keys.md [R3] ((6) N5, (7) row B2, the switch section), and, as 114 leaves it, backup.rs's seal_key, reading_key, key_name, gpg_by and put_new_object.

Why. The owner's two backup keys (lead-mac 10:01). Since 114, the store seals with the sealing key's file, derives its segment names from that key, and every object it PUTs says which key sealed it (x-amz-meta-spawn-seal). It does not yet read by key. With SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY=k2 and a last manifest sealed with k1, it opens that manifest with k2 and fails. And if it could open it, it would build on segments named under another key. So the store's switch to k2 (a drop-in, a lead step) waits for this objective: the design's switch step 3 says "only after 114, 115 and 116 have all landed" (rev-g). Until then the store is never given k2.

Required behaviour (store.rs only):
- The newest manifest's key is the name its object carries in `x-amz-meta-spawn-seal`, read with backup::key_name. An object with no header is k1's: every store object from before 114 has none.
- When that key is the sealing key, everything is as today: segments are reused, and unchanged, grown and whole files are as now.
- When it is another key, and that key's file is on this host (backup::reading_key, mode 600):
  - put opens that manifest with its own key and takes its generation (the new manifest is generation + 1, as today);
  - put never names one of its segments again (their names are another key's HMACs) and puts every file whole under the sealing key: unchanged 0, grown 0, segments_found 0 for that run, whole = files;
  - get, list and verify read that manifest, and rebuild its segments, with its own key and its own naming key;
  - plan decides as put does: every file is to be sent whole (rev-e's F1).
- When that key's file is not on this host: the run refuses with exit 2, saying "the last manifest is sealed with <name>; its key file <path> is not on this host" (the path as 114's reasons give it). It writes no object and no record, and never starts a fresh chain over a manifest it could not read.
- backup.stored gains `"sealed_with": "<the sealing key's name>"`, which 115 lets the schema take.
- A name is the only thing printed about a key. No key's content reaches an output, a record or an argv.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/store.rs only. The PUT's header is 114's (put_new_object), so this objective changes nothing in backup.rs. One crate, about 220 lines (the throwaway's size is in its proof; most of it moves list and verify out of command into functions of their own, to keep command under clippy's length).

After: 114 (the header, seal_key, reading_key, key_name, gpg_by) and 115 (backup.stored takes sealed_with).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/116.sh. Black box against 104's local R2 stand-in ONLY: a second instance whose bucket is the scenario's own work bucket (bb116-work), under locktest/ prefixes. It reads neither r2-store.env nor r2.env, makes no call off the host, and never names a real or keep bucket. It runs on its own database, scratch HOME, GNUPGHOME and key directory, with made-up keys; k1 starts under its old name.
(1) Before the switch: a put under two prefixes A and B exits 0, each record saying sealed_with k1.
(2) After the switch (backup.key renamed backup.key.k1, backup.key.k2 made, SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY=k2): `spawn store plan` under A says 2 files whole and all their bytes to send. A put under A exits 0. Its record is {sealed_with k2, files 2, whole 2, unchanged 0, grown 0, segments_found 0}. Its manifest is generation 2, opens with k2, and names no segment of A's k1 manifest. Every segment it names, and the manifest, says k2. A second k2 put with nothing changed is as before two keys: unchanged 2, whole 0, segments_written 0, generation 3.
(3) With k1's file away: `spawn store get` restores a file of A's k2 manifest byte for byte, and `spawn store verify` exits 0.
(4) Still with k1's file away: a put under B (last manifest k1's) exits 2 with the reason above, writes no object and records nothing.
(4b) With k1 back and SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY=k2, B's newest manifest (k1's) is read with k1: get restores a file of it byte for byte, verify exits 0, and list names it.
(5) With k1 back and B's manifest stripped of its header: a put under B with k2 exits 0, generation 2, every file whole, sealed_with k2.
(6) No key's passphrase and no R2 secret is in any output or record.
114.sh and 115.sh must keep passing. check-tests.sh and check-clippy.sh must pass.
